column1: # RECIPE_MEMORY.tsv - append-only lesson memory of recipe mat-sortable-processor-20261107 (RELOCATE_MAT_SORTABLE_PROCESSOR): one row per lesson, appended in the same commit as the correction.

column4: the census row names the crate's hash-pinned postimages (5ac862a5d0c7 / 91faab90f251, 2026-10-14); develop carries the heads extended by the structural-recovery and @SortDependency crates of 2026-11-01 (095ac09526a5, 671 lines; f43741f44b5c, 502 lines): relocate the develop-live heads, by git log --no-renames over the owning directory of the blobless clone (never --follow, never a tree grep)

the processor reaches its annotations by canonical-name strings and needs java.compiler only, so it is a compile-time module of the m3/compiler family (static-use pattern) with m3-collections in test scope for the fixtures; putting it in m3/collections would have added java.compiler to the collection module inside peer 22's lane

derived from m3/compiler/static-use/recipe/static-use-plan-20261107/relocate.py v1 by a scripted exact-anchor derivation (23 anchors) that adds the REPLACE row kind: a contiguous donor block pinned by sha256 and line count, replaced by declared lines ('-' removes it), counted in PROVENANCE.tsv as declared_replaces; needed because the held members are multi-line blocks whose first line ("if (hasSignal) {") occurs twice in the file, which a DROP row refuses

a REPLACE row's replacement text carries its newlines as the two characters backslash-n; the Bash tool collapses doubled backslashes, so a row written through a shell heredoc split into three physical lines and read_map refused the map ("not enough values to unpack"): write such rows with the Edit tool (or a script written by Write), never through a shell command
column5: relocate run 2: ValueError in read_map; run 3: FILE CHANGED declared_replaces=3

column4: a processor class in an exported module package needs an explicit public constructor or -Xlint:missing-explicit-ctor fails -Werror; the donor (no module) has an implicit one; the REPLACE row of the held field capabilityEmitted writes the explicit constructor, no lint category is disabled on the module build

the donor contract is red at develop 56cbdc631259 against the donor processor ("No processor claimed any of these annotations" under -Xlint:all -Werror, since process returns false on purpose); the relocated contract disables that one lint category by a REPLACE row and the differential prints the donor run as BASELINE_RED; a baseline defect is reported in HANDOFF.tsv, never hidden and never "fixed" in the processor

the first donor / relocated comparison differed in 25 DIAG lines: javac reports element positions, and on a one-line fixture every element after @Sortable vs @M3Sortable shifts by two columns per annotation; every fixture annotation now stands on its own line (oneAnnotationPerLine) and the import line is padded to a fixed width
column5: differential-1.log (DIFFERENT, 50 diff lines, columns only); differential-2.log IDENTICAL 82,403 bytes

column4: the donor processor also runs its capability emitter (held lane): extra <Type>M3Capabilities companions and "invalid M3 capability schema" diagnostics on the donor side, and the held stableSignalOrder block in signal companions; the oracle declares exactly these three masks (DECISION.tsv S7) and -proc:only so the companions are compared as source without the held MatIntOrder owner on the class path

jdk_naming.py rewrites .sh / .py / .java text, so a donor module path (synexia-mat-collections/...) or the donor package in a Javadoc sentence is a rewrite: the differential reads the donor annotation package and its source root from the map's EXTERNAL row (TSV ledgers are lineage, not rewritten) and the oracle Javadoc names "the donor's annotation package"
column5: naming plan 1: rewrites=2 (KEBAB=2 PKG=1 PKG_PATH=1); plan 2: rewrites=0

column4: git add -A of the module directory staged target/ (no .gitignore covers m3/compiler/*/target): stage explicit paths (recipe, src, pom.xml) and check git status before the commit

verify.sh passes paths in the MSYS form (/s/...) that a JVM class path entry does not understand: the first verify run compiled the relocated fixtures without jdk.m3.collections (package does not exist) while the hand run with S:/... passed; differential.sh now normalizes the m3-collections class-path argument (directory or jar) with pwd -W
